research_scope: Source-free, mathematically type-aware audit of shared prerequisites; no source edits and no broad Batch143 population.

aliases.reason: Topological separatedness requires X×_Y X, the self-pullback of f:X→Y. Universally closed continuous maps require X×_Y Z, an ordinary topological pullback. The first is the specialization Z=X with both arrows f; the subspace-topology pullback construction is identical, but diagonal closedness and universal closedness remain distinct.

An element integral over an ideal is tested by a positive-degree monic polynomial P(T), and étale/minimal-polynomial definitions use a univariate polynomial with leading coefficient 1. The monic predicate is shared; positive degree and coefficient conditions a_j∈I^{d-j} stay parent-specific.

The universally closed topological map and universally closed scheme morphism definitions each invoke that a particular continuous base-change map sends closed subsets to closed subsets. That is the same closed-map prerequisite; schemes vs arbitrary topological spaces and universal quantification over base changes remain parent-specific.

Discrete-time and real-time martingale definitions both use L^1 integrability of each real random variable, E|X_t|<∞; the index symbol and its range (natural vs nonnegative real time) do not alter the integrability predicate. Filtration and martingale equalities remain separate.

Topological closure and irreducible-space sources both require F closed in X exactly when X\F is open in its topology. Neither assumes a metric or Hausdorff space, so these are identical general closed-subset prerequisites, distinct from a closed map or closed immersion.
